destinations.name: Angkor Wat
destinations.shortDescription: The world's largest religious monument
destinations.longDescription: Built in the early 12th century by King Suryavarman II, Angkor Wat is the largest religious structure ever built and the centrepiece of the Angkor Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its five towers represent the peaks of Mount Meru, and the outer gallery walls carry nearly 600 metres of bas-relief carvings. Sunrise viewed from across the western moat is the classic Cambodian postcard image.
destinations.address: Angkor Archaeological Park, Krong Siem Reap

destinations.name: Bayon Temple
destinations.shortDescription: Temple of 200 serene stone faces
destinations.longDescription: At the exact centre of the walled city of Angkor Thom stands Bayon, built by Jayavarman VII at the end of the 12th century. Its towers are carved with more than 200 enormous serene faces that seem to follow you as you move through the upper terrace. The lower gallery reliefs show scenes of everyday Khmer life rather than only gods and kings.
destinations.address: Angkor Thom, Angkor Archaeological Park

destinations.name: Ta Prohm
destinations.shortDescription: Ancient temple swallowed by jungle
destinations.longDescription: Ta Prohm has been deliberately left much as it was found, with giant silk-cotton and strangler fig roots prying apart the sandstone galleries. The interplay of tree and stone makes it the most atmospheric temple in the park, and it became widely known internationally after appearing in adventure films shot on location.
destinations.address: Angkor Archaeological Park, Krong Siem Reap

destinations.name: Banteay Srei
destinations.shortDescription: The pink sandstone jewel of Khmer art
destinations.longDescription: Roughly 35 km north-east of the main Angkor group, Banteay Srei was consecrated in 967 AD and is built from a hard red sandstone that holds astonishingly fine detail. The carving here is the most intricate in Cambodia, which is why it is often called the citadel of women. It is small, so it rewards a slow visit rather than a quick stop.
destinations.address: Banteay Srei District, Siem Reap Province

destinations.name: Kampong Phluk Floating Village
destinations.shortDescription: Stilted village on the Tonle Sap lake
destinations.longDescription: A cluster of villages where every house stands on wooden stilts six to ten metres tall, built to survive the annual rise and fall of the Tonle Sap. In the wet season boats glide between the houses and through a flooded mangrove forest; in the dry season the stilts tower over dusty ground. Going with a community-based operator keeps more of the fee in the village.
destinations.address: Kampong Phluk, Prasat Bakong District
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: August - November, when water is high

destinations.name: Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda
destinations.shortDescription: Historic landmark in Phnom Penh
destinations.longDescription: The official residence of the King of Cambodia since 1866. Visitors can see the Throne Hall with its tiered Khmer roof, the Napoleon III Pavilion, and the neighbouring Silver Pagoda, whose floor is laid with more than five thousand solid silver tiles. Shoulders and knees must be covered to enter the grounds.
destinations.address: Samdach Sothearos Blvd, Khan Daun Penh, Phnom Penh

destinations.name: National Museum of Cambodia
destinations.shortDescription: The country's finest Khmer sculpture collection
destinations.longDescription: Housed in a terracotta-coloured pavilion built in 1920, the museum holds the world's largest collection of Khmer art, spanning pre-Angkorian bronzes through to post-Angkorian ceramics. Visiting before a trip to Angkor makes the temples much easier to read, since many of the original statues from those sites are displayed here.
destinations.address: Street 13, Khan Daun Penh, Phnom Penh

destinations.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
destinations.shortDescription: Memorial museum in a former school
destinations.longDescription: A former secondary school that the Khmer Rouge converted into Security Prison 21. It is preserved as a memorial and museum documenting the period between 1975 and 1979, and the audio guide is widely regarded as one of the best in the region. The subject matter is heavy, so plan something gentle for afterwards.
destinations.address: Street 113, Boeng Keng Kang, Phnom Penh

destinations.name: Choeung Ek Memorial
destinations.shortDescription: Memorial site south of the capital
destinations.longDescription: A quiet field about 15 km from central Phnom Penh, now a place of remembrance marked by a memorial stupa. It is usually visited together with Tuol Sleng, and most travellers find the audio guide, narrated in part by survivors, the most affecting part of the visit. Dress and behave as you would at any memorial.
destinations.address: Sangkat Cheung Aek, Dangkao District, Phnom Penh

destinations.name: Wat Phnom
destinations.shortDescription: The hilltop temple the city is named after
destinations.longDescription: Standing on the only hill in Phnom Penh, this pagoda was founded in 1372 and gives the capital its name. A naga-flanked staircase leads up to the vihara, and the shaded park around the base is a pleasant place to sit. It is a short walk from the riverside and easy to fit into a city afternoon.
destinations.address: Norodom Blvd, Khan Daun Penh, Phnom Penh

destinations.name: Central Market
destinations.shortDescription: Art deco landmark full of stalls
destinations.longDescription: Phsar Thmei opened in 1937 and its enormous ochre dome with four radiating wings is one of the finest art deco buildings in South East Asia. Inside, the central rotunda sells jewellery and watches, while the wings run to fabric, electronics, souvenirs and a busy food section. Prices are negotiable, so agree a figure before handing anything over.
destinations.address: Kampuchea Krom Blvd, Khan Daun Penh, Phnom Penh

destinations.name: Koh Rong
destinations.shortDescription: Beautiful beaches and clear water
destinations.longDescription: Cambodia's second-largest island, ringed by long stretches of white sand and warm shallow water. Long Set Beach and Sok San are the quieter options, while the pier village has the bulk of the guesthouses and bars. Night swims can reveal bioluminescent plankton when conditions are right. Speedboats run from Sihanoukville in about 45 minutes.
destinations.address: Koh Rong Island, Preah Sihanouk Province

destinations.name: Koh Rong Sanloem
destinations.shortDescription: Quiet island bays and calm sea
destinations.longDescription: Smaller and sleepier than its neighbour, Koh Rong Sanloem is built around a handful of separate bays. Saracen Bay is the wide crescent with most of the accommodation, while Lazy Beach and Sunset Beach are reached by a short jungle trail across the island. There are no cars and electricity is often limited to set hours.
destinations.address: Koh Rong Sanloem, Preah Sihanouk Province

destinations.name: Otres Beach
destinations.shortDescription: Relaxed mainland beach strip
destinations.longDescription: A few kilometres south of central Sihanoukville, Otres is a long straight beach with a row of low-key beach bars and guesthouses behind it. It is the easiest sand to reach on the mainland coast if you do not have time for the islands, and sunsets over the water are reliably good.
destinations.address: Otres, Krong Preah Sihanouk

destinations.name: Bokor Mountain
destinations.shortDescription: Scenic mountain destination
destinations.longDescription: A cool highland plateau inside Preah Monivong National Park, reached by a well-surfaced switchback road from Kampot. The draw is the combination of an abandoned French colonial hill station, the Popokvil waterfall, forest trails and long views over the Gulf of Thailand. Mist rolls in fast, so go in the morning for the clearest outlook.
destinations.address: Preah Monivong Bokor National Park, Kampot Province

destinations.name: La Plantation Pepper Farm
destinations.shortDescription: Kampot pepper farm with free tours
destinations.longDescription: Kampot pepper carries a protected geographical indication and is prized by chefs worldwide. This farm runs free guided walks explaining how the vines are grown and hand-sorted, ending in a tasting where you can compare black, red and white peppercorns. The setting among karst hills is a large part of the appeal.
destinations.address: Chhuk District, Kampot Province

destinations.name: Kep Crab Market
destinations.shortDescription: Famous seafood destination
destinations.longDescription: A row of seaside stalls where vendors pull blue swimmer crab straight from baskets submerged at the water's edge. Buy by weight and take it to one of the adjoining grills, or eat at a restaurant on the pier. Crab fried with fresh green Kampot peppercorns is the dish everyone comes for.
destinations.address: Kep Crab Market, Krong Kep

destinations.name: Kep National Park
destinations.shortDescription: Coastal jungle loop trail
destinations.longDescription: One of Cambodia's smallest national parks, wrapped around the hill behind Kep town. An eight-kilometre loop trail circles it, with clearly signed side paths to viewpoints looking out over the sea and Rabbit Island. It is walkable in a morning and the shade makes it manageable even in warm weather.
destinations.address: Kep National Park, Krong Kep

destinations.name: Phnom Sampeau
destinations.shortDescription: Limestone hill with a bat cave exodus
destinations.longDescription: A limestone outcrop outside Battambang topped by a golden pagoda and a series of caves, some of which are memorials to the Khmer Rouge period. At dusk, millions of bats stream out of a cave mouth in a continuous ribbon that lasts close to half an hour, and there is a small viewing area set up for it.
destinations.address: Phnom Sampeau, Banan District, Battambang

destinations.name: Preah Vihear Temple
destinations.shortDescription: Cliff-top temple on the Dangrek range
destinations.longDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage temple built along an 800-metre axis on a promontory of the Dangrek Mountains, ending at a cliff with a 500-metre drop and an enormous view across the plains. Its remoteness means far fewer visitors than Angkor. The final ascent is steep, so most people transfer to a local pickup or moto for the last stretch.
destinations.address: Preah Vihear Temple, Choam Khsant District
destinations.entryFee: Around $10 plus transport up the hill

destinations.name: Kirirom National Park
destinations.shortDescription: Pine forest highland park near the capital
destinations.longDescription: The first national park declared in Cambodia, sitting at around 700 metres and noticeably cooler than the lowlands. Pine forest, waterfalls, small lakes and viewpoints toward the Cardamom Mountains make it a popular weekend escape roughly two hours from Phnom Penh. Mountain biking and camping are both well established here.
destinations.address: Preah Suramarit Kossamak National Park, Kampong Speu

destinations.name: Bou Sra Waterfall
destinations.shortDescription: Two-tier waterfall in the eastern highlands
destinations.longDescription: The best known waterfall in Mondulkiri, dropping in two large tiers through dense forest in the province's east. A walkway and a zipline cross the gorge, and the surrounding area is home to Bunong communities and several ethical elephant sanctuaries that can be combined into the same trip.
destinations.address: Bou Sra, Pech Chreada District, Mondulkiri
